# ADR-0013: Motion with native `animate.enter` and CSS on duration tokens, enter-only step transition, reduced motion by construction

## Context and Problem Statement

US-04 asks for an animated step indicator, a transition between steps, hover, focus, active and
disabled states, soft validation feedback, skeletons while Strapi loads, interactive plan cards
and summary micro-animations, all honouring `prefers-reduced-motion` ("no movement if the user asks
for it"), and asks the ADR to propose the library and "justify bundle weight and maintenance"
(story; US-04-BR-09, BR-10). The step transition must not put two pages, two `main` or two `h1`
elements in the document at once, and focus must still land on the arriving `h1` (US-04-AC-14;
ADR-0001). This ADR picks the mechanism, the motion tokens, the step transition and how reduced
motion is applied and tested (US-04-Q-14, Q-16).

## Decision Drivers

- D1. No movement under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`: every computed animation and transition
  duration 0 s and no running animation (US-04-BR-10, AC-17).
- D2. One page in the DOM during a step change, focus on the arriving `h1`, document title as today
  (US-04-AC-14; ADR-0001 "Focus on step change"; ADR-0009 heading outline).
- D3. Bundle weight and maintenance justified (story); budgets kept (spec §9); exact versions and a
  permissive licence for anything new (US-04-BR-14).
- D4. Animate `transform` and `opacity` only (spec §9, Performance).
- D5. Durations and easings are tokens (US-04-BR-01, ADR-0010).
- D6. Motion never interferes with announcements: role `alert`/`status` text is in the DOM at once
  (spec §8; US-04-Q-16: no counting-up of numbers).
- D7. Restraint: motion answers a person's action; one orchestrated moment beats scattered effects
  (vendored `frontend-design` skill, adopted with CLAUDE.md §5 overrides).

## Considered Options

1. **A. Native `animate.enter` / `animate.leave` + CSS keyframes and transitions** on duration and
   easing tokens; no animation library.
2. **B. Router `withViewTransitions()`** (View Transitions API) for the step change, plus CSS for
   everything else.
3. **C. An animation library**: Motion (`motion` 14.14.0) or GSAP (`gsap` 3.15.1), driven from
   `(animate.enter)` / `(animate.leave)` callbacks.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"A. Native `animate.enter` + CSS on tokens"**, because it costs zero bytes and no
dependency (D3), is stable public API in 22.3.0, covers every effect the spec lists with
`transform` and `opacity` (D4), and lets reduced motion be guaranteed by construction rather than by
overrides (D1). An enter-only page animation keeps exactly one page in the DOM (D2). B covers only
route changes, so it would be a second mechanism next to A, and it became public API only in this
very version. C adds 71–74 kB raw per library for effects CSS already does, and GSAP's licence is
not an OSI licence.

### What is decided

#### 1. Motion tokens (in `tokens.css`, ADR-0010)

| Token | Value | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `--duration-fast` | 120ms | hover, press, focus ring, error fade-in, panel close (exits are faster than entries) |
| `--duration-base` | 200ms | step enter, panel open, bottom-sheet slide, indicator fill, segmented control |
| `--duration-slow` | 320ms | confirmation check-circle; upper bound of any single transition (AC-14) |
| `--delay-stagger-1` … `--delay-stagger-4` | 0ms, 50ms, 100ms, 150ms | summary sections (total ≤ 150 + 200 = 350 ms, under Q-16's 400 ms) |
| `--duration-shimmer` | 1400ms | skeleton shimmer loop |
| `--duration-spin` | 800ms | "Pagar" processing spinner |
| `--ease-out` | `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` | entries |
| `--ease-in` | `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)` | exits |
| `--ease-standard` | `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` | state changes (colour, border, glow) |
| `--motion-rise` | 0.5rem (8 px) | step enter and panel offset |

No bounce or overshoot curves. Under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` every `--duration-*`
and `--delay-*` token is `0ms` (a second line of defence; see §3).

#### 2. Where motion is used (and where it is not)

| Effect | Mechanism | Property |
|---|---|---|
| Step change | `animate.enter="page-enter"` on the root element of each routed page; **no** `animate.leave` | opacity 0 → 1, translateY(`--motion-rise`) → 0, `--duration-base`, `--ease-out` |
| Step indicator fill | CSS transition on the progress bar | `transform: scaleX()` |
| Select panel open | `animate.enter` on the panel | opacity, translateY(−`--motion-rise`/2) |
| Bottom sheet open | `animate.enter` on the sheet | translateY(100%) → 0 |
| Panel close | instant by default; `animate.leave` only if the developer confirms it runs when the CDK overlay detaches (no AC needs it) | opacity |
| Error text | `animate.enter="error-enter"` | opacity only (no shake); the text is in the DOM, inside `role="alert"`, from the first frame (D6) |
| Hover / active / chosen plan | CSS transitions | `border-color`, `box-shadow`, `background-color` (paint), and a 2 px lift on hover only for `(hover: hover)` pointers |
| Skeleton shimmer | keyframes on a pseudo-element | `transform: translateX()` |
| "Pagar" spinner | keyframes on the icon | `transform: rotate()` |
| Summary sections | `animate.enter` with `--delay-stagger-n` by `:nth-of-type` | opacity, translateY |
| Confirmation | `animate.enter` on the check-circle | scale 0.85 → 1 and opacity, `--duration-slow` (the single orchestrated moment of the flow) |

Not animated: prices and numbers (no counting up, D6), headings, the country chooser list, text in
live regions. Hover transitions are colour and shadow changes, not motion, except the 2 px lift
(D7: "hover transitions on every card" read as generated; the plan cards are the one place where a
lift explains "this is clickable", US-04-BR-09).

**Step transition, why one page only.** The router removes the leaving component and inserts the
arriving one in the same change; with no `animate.leave`, Angular does not keep the old element.
Only the arriving page animates in, so there is never a second `h1` or `main` (AC-14). Focus moves
to the arriving `h1` as today: opacity and transform do not affect focus or the accessibility tree.

#### 3. Reduced motion, by construction (D1)

- In every style file except `tokens.css`, each `animation`, `animation-*`, `transition` and
  `transition-*` declaration sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { … }`.
  Under `reduce` no animation or transition is declared at all: computed durations are the initial
  `0s`, `document.getAnimations()` is empty, and states (colour, border, icon, text) still change,
  instantly. This keeps feedback while removing movement, a principle restated from
  `pbakaus/impeccable` `animate.md` (Apache-2.0, credited per EVAL-004), and it avoids the global
  `0.01ms !important` kill switch that the same source flags.
- `animate.enter` classes therefore have no animation under `reduce`; Angular reads the computed
  styles, finds none, and removes the class at once (`@angular/core@22.3.0`
  `determineLongestAnimation` falls back to computed styles when `getAnimations()` is empty;
  `MAX_ANIMATION_TIMEOUT` default 4000 ms is never reached).
- The duration tokens are also set to `0ms` under `reduce` in `tokens.css`, so a declaration that
  escapes the `no-preference` block still has no duration.
- **CDK overlays and dialogs** (ADR-0012) are created with `disableAnimations: true`. The CDK's own
  backdrop has `transition: opacity 400ms` and, under reduced motion, `transition-duration: 1ms`
  (`@angular/cdk@22.3.0` overlay styles), which would fail AC-17's "0s"; with
  `disableAnimations`, the CDK adds `cdk-overlay-backdrop-noop-animation` (`transition: none`). Our
  own backdrop fade, if any, is a token transition inside the `no-preference` block in
  `styles.css`.
- The spinner stops under `reduce`; "Procesando pago…" (US-03) remains the feedback.

#### 4. Tests (AC-14, AC-17)

- **Static guard** (extends ADR-0010's guard): outside `tokens.css`, no `animation`/`transition`
  declaration outside a `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` block; durations, delays and
  easings only as `var(--duration-*)`, `var(--delay-*)`, `var(--ease-*)`; `tokens.css` sets every
  `--duration-*` and `--delay-*` to `0ms` under `reduce`; every `createOverlayRef`,
  `cdkConnectedOverlay` and `Dialog.open` call passes `disableAnimations: true` (a grep on the
  production sources).
- **E2E AC-17**: a Playwright context with `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` walks step 1 (with "Ciudad"
  open and the calendar open), step 2, the summary and the confirmation; on each state it asserts
  that every element's computed `animationDuration` and `transitionDuration` list only `0s`, and
  `document.getAnimations()` is empty.
- **E2E AC-14**: with motion allowed, a `MutationObserver` installed before "Continuar" records the
  maximum number of `h1` and `main` elements seen during navigation (expected 1 and 1); then focus
  is on "Elige tu plan" and the title is unchanged; the page's enter animation reports a duration
  ≤ `--duration-slow` through `getAnimations()`.

### Consequences

- Good, because no dependency, no bytes, no licence question (D3); `animate.enter` is
  `@publicApi 20.2` in `@angular/core@22.3.0` and the vendored skill's own guidance for v20.2+.
- Good, because reduced motion is a property of how styles are written, enforced by a guard, not a
  late override that can be missed (D1).
- Good, because one page is ever in the DOM (D2), and focus and announcements are untouched (D6).
- Bad, because the old page disappears without an exit animation, so the change is a cut followed by
  a fade-in, less fluid than a cross-fade — mitigation: the fade is short (200 ms) and the step
  indicator fill gives continuity; B can be added later as an enhancement if the human wants a
  cross-fade (see *Revisit*).
- Bad, because closing a panel inside a CDK overlay may not run `animate.leave` (the overlay detaches
  its content) — mitigation: panels close instantly unless the developer proves the leave runs; no
  AC requires a close animation.
- Bad, because writing every animation inside a media block is a discipline — mitigation: the guard
  fails the gate otherwise.
- Neutral: the first page load also plays `page-enter` once; that is the single page-load moment.

### Strongest argument against

The View Transitions route (B) gives a real two-state transition with one line,
`withViewTransitions()`: the browser snapshots the old page and cross-fades it into the new one,
while the live DOM still holds only the new page (so AC-14 holds too). It can even morph the step
indicator between steps with a `view-transition-name`, which is the "animated step indicator" the
story asks for, and browsers without support simply skip it. Enter-only CSS is a hard cut followed
by a fade, the kind of generic "fade-and-rise" the `frontend-design` skill calls a tell of generated
pages.

**Why we accept it:** B only animates route changes, so the panels, errors, skeletons, cards,
spinner and confirmation still need A: two mechanisms, two reduced-motion paths (B also needs
`skipTransition()` or `::view-transition-*` rules under `reduce`, and its pseudo-element
animations show up in `document.getAnimations()` during AC-17). `withViewTransitions` is tagged
`@publicApi 22.3` in the 22.3.0 typings, so it has been public API only since the release we pin,
three days before this ADR. The fade-in here is brief and paired with the indicator fill, and the
one orchestrated moment is the confirmation, as the skill advises. B stays a contained later
enhancement on top of A.

### Confirmation

- Static guard rules of §4 (US-04-AC-17, AC-01).
- E2E `us-04-design-system.spec.ts`: AC-14 and AC-17 as in §4.
- Component tests (AC-15): skeletons are `aria-hidden`, the loading text stays in its live region.
- HC3: the human checks the motion with the OS setting on and off (AC-23).
- `frontend/package.json` contains no `motion`, `gsap`, `@angular/animations` or other animation
  dependency (dependency list guard of ADR-0010).

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### A. Native `animate.enter` / `animate.leave` + CSS (chosen)

- Good, because zero bytes and zero dependencies; stable API since 20.2.
- Good, because every effect is plain CSS on tokens, and reduced motion is enforced statically.
- Bad, because there is no exit for the leaving page (by design) and limited choreography.

### B. Router `withViewTransitions()`

`@angular/router@22.3.0` typings: `withViewTransitions` tagged `@publicApi 22.3`.

- Good, because a true cross-fade (or a morph of named elements) with one line; one page in the DOM.
- Good, because progressive: unsupported browsers navigate without a transition.
- Bad, because it covers route changes only; everything else still needs A.
- Bad, because reduced motion needs its own handling, and its animations appear in
  `document.getAnimations()` while running.
- Bad, because it became public API in 22.3.0 itself.

### C. Motion 14.14.0 or GSAP 3.15.1

Verified on npm (2026-11-21): `motion@14.14.0` MIT, unpacked 1.0 MB; `gsap@3.15.1` licence
"Standard 'no charge' license: https://gsap.com/standard-license", unpacked 6.3 MB. Measured on a
throwaway build (baseline initial 381.44 kB raw / 98.94 kB transfer): `import { animate } from
'motion'` **+74.10 kB raw / +23.97 kB transfer**; `motion/mini` **+8.92 / +2.71**; `gsap`
**+71.36 / +25.00**.

- Good, because springs, timelines and sequencing beyond CSS.
- Bad, because nothing in the spec needs them: every listed effect is a CSS transform or opacity.
- Bad, because the weight is real (motion, gsap) or the features are what CSS already has
  (motion/mini); one more dependency to upgrade.
- Bad, because GSAP's licence is not an OSI permissive licence, so US-04-BR-14 would need a human
  exception.

## Spec impact (reported to the orchestrator; the spec is not edited here)

1. **US-04-Q-16** "confirmation check-circle draw": a stroke "draw" animates `stroke-dashoffset`,
   which is neither transform nor opacity (spec §9). This ADR uses a scale-and-fade instead. If the
   human wants the draw, spec §9 should allow paint-only SVG stroke properties.
2. **US-04-AC-01 / BR-01** allowed media conditions: the guard of ADR-0010 must also accept the
   `(hover: hover)` media feature used for the card lift.
3. **US-04-AC-17** "document.getAnimations() returns no running animation": with §3 it returns no
   animation at all; the scenario may assert the stronger "empty".

## More Information

- **Verified on 2026-11-21** (installed `frontend/node_modules`, packed `@angular/cdk@22.3.0`, npm
  registry, a throwaway build in a temporary directory; nothing installed in the project):
  - `@angular/core@22.3.0` typings: `AnimationCallbackEvent` and the `animate.enter`/`animate.leave`
    types are `@publicApi 20.2`; runtime in `fesm2022/_debug_node-chunk.mjs`
    (`determineLongestAnimation`, `MAX_ANIMATION_TIMEOUT` default 4000).
  - `@angular/router@22.3.0` typings: `withViewTransitions` `@publicApi 22.3`.
  - `@angular/cdk@22.3.0`: `OverlayConfig.disableAnimations`, `DialogConfig.disableAnimations`;
    overlay styles: backdrop `transition: opacity 400ms …`, reduced-motion `transition-duration: 1ms`,
    `.cdk-overlay-backdrop-noop-animation { transition: none }`.
  - Bundle numbers in *Pros and Cons* C.
- **Credit:** "reduce movement, keep feedback", "exits faster than entries", "no bounce by reflex",
  "animate transform and opacity" are restated from `pbakaus/impeccable` at `0a4e72a` (`animate.md`,
  Apache-2.0), as EVAL-004 allows.
- **Skill notes:** the vendored `angular-animations.md` recommends `animate.enter`/`animate.leave`
  for v20.2+ (consistent); `route-animations.md` describes `withViewTransitions` (option B, not
  chosen). `@angular/animations` is not added.
- **Related ADRs:** ADR-0010 (tokens, guard), ADR-0012 (CDK overlays and dialog), ADR-0001 (focus on
  the arriving heading).
- **Revisit when:** the human asks for a cross-fade between steps (add B on top of A, with its own
  reduced-motion handling and an AC-17 row), or a later story needs choreography CSS cannot express.

9	# ADR-0012: Accessible custom select and date picker on `@angular/aria` and `@angular/cdk`, bound to Signal Forms (amends ADR-0004)
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	US-04 replaces the browser's `<select>` and `<input type="date">` of step 1 with design-system
14	controls: a select with an icon, search for long lists and the selected option marked, and a date
15	field that accepts typed dd/mm/aaaa and opens a calendar with month and year navigation and days
16	disabled by the `minAge` rule (US-04-BR-05, BR-06). The story requires them to be "built on
17	accessible primitives, not from scratch: Angular CDK (Overlay, Listbox, a11y) or `@angular/aria`
18	if it is stable in our version", with the WAI-ARIA combobox/listbox and date picker dialog
19	patterns, a bottom sheet on mobile, and validations and stored values unchanged. ADR-0004
20	(Accepted) chose Signal Forms with **native controls** (its driver D7) and its implementation note
21	makes `syncNative` the only writer of number and date keys, built on `validity.badInput`. This ADR
22	picks the primitives, defines how the controls plug into Signal Forms and the shared validation
23	core, and amends ADR-0004 where it assumed native controls (US-04-Q-04, Q-05, Q-11..Q-13).
24	
25	## Decision Drivers
26	
27	- D1. WAI-ARIA APG patterns: combobox with listbox popup (select-only and list autocomplete), date
28	  picker dialog; full keyboard map of US-04-AC-06, AC-09; focus trapped and returned; polite
29	  announcements (story; US-04-BR-05, BR-06, BR-13).
30	- D2. Built on primitives, not from scratch; exact versions, permissive licence; `@angular/cdk`
31	  equal to the framework version (story; US-04-BR-14; CLAUDE.md §4).
32	- D3. Same validation, same stored values, same error timing and focus target as before
33	  (US-04-BR-07, AC-11; ADR-0004: string editing model, `validateField` as the only rule engine,
34	  `touched && invalid`, `focusBoundControl()` on a failed submit; ADR-0003 stored shape).
35	- D4. The labelled, focused element is an `<input>` or `<button>` targeted by the field's
36	  `<label for>`, so `label.control`, `getByLabel` and the existing `aria-*` bindings keep working
37	  (US-04-BR-05, Q-04 constraint, Q-06, §11.1).
38	- D5. Typed date dd/mm/aaaa for every country, independent of the browser locale, stored as ISO;
39	  unreadable text behaves like the former `badInput` (US-04-BR-06, Q-05; US-01-BR-01, AC-09 note).
40	- D6. Disabled days come from the same pure validator, no second implementation (US-04-BR-06).
41	- D7. Panels: popover on wide screens, bottom sheet below 600 px; 44 × 44 px targets; no horizontal
42	  scroll (US-04-BR-11, AC-12, Q-13).
43	- D8. Bundle budgets (`angular.json`: initial 500 kB warning) kept or justified (spec §9).
44	- D9. Testable in jsdom component tests and Playwright e2e by role and label, never by class
45	  (story; spec §11.1).
46	
47	## Considered Options
48	
49	1. **A. `@angular/aria` 22.3.0 for the combobox, listbox and year list, with `@angular/cdk`
50	   22.3.0** for overlay positioning, the calendar dialog (focus trap and return), live
51	   announcements and breakpoints; the calendar grid's date navigation as a pure function.
52	2. **B. `@angular/cdk` 22.3.0 only**: Overlay, `ActiveDescendantKeyManager` (and `cdk/listbox` for
53	   the year list), `Dialog`, `LiveAnnouncer`; the combobox roles, states and key handling wired by
54	   hand around the key manager.
55	3. **C. Angular Material 22.3.0** (`mat-select` / `mat-autocomplete`, `mat-datepicker` with its
56	   multi-year view), restyled to the design system.
57	
58	Building the widgets from scratch is excluded by the story.
59	
60	## Decision Outcome
61	
62	Chosen option: **"A. `@angular/aria` + `@angular/cdk`"**, because `@angular/aria` is stable at
63	22.x (the developer-preview tag was removed in 22.0.0) and implements the APG combobox wiring that
64	option B would have us write by hand (role and states, `aria-activedescendant`, key relay,
65	typeahead, close on focus-out), which is closest to "from scratch" (D1, D2). It works on an
66	`<input>` (editable) and on a `<button>` (select-only), so the labelled element stays a labelable
67	native element (D4). The CDK supplies what `@angular/aria` does not have: overlay positioning with
68	a bottom sheet, a modal dialog with focus trap and return, and the live announcer. Material (C)
69	would bring a complete date picker but a select host that a `<label for>` cannot target and a
70	theming system that competes with our token tiers.
71	
72	### What is decided
73	
74	#### 1. Packages (new dependencies)
75	
76	| Package | Version | Licence | Peers (verified) | Why |
77	|---|---|---|---|---|
78	| `@angular/cdk` | **22.3.0** | MIT | `@angular/core`, `common`, `forms`, `platform-browser` `^22.0.0 \|\| ^23.0.0`; `rxjs ^6.5.3 \|\| ^7.4.0`; deps `tslib`, `parse5` | Overlay, Dialog, a11y (`LiveAnnouncer`), layout (`BreakpointObserver`) |
79	| `@angular/aria` | **22.3.0** | MIT | `@angular/cdk` **`22.3.0`** (exact), `@angular/core ^22.0.0 \|\| ^23.0.0` | `Combobox`, `ComboboxPopup`, `ComboboxWidget`, `Listbox`, `Option` |
80	
81	Both equal the framework version; an Angular upgrade (CLAUDE.md §4) moves all `@angular/*`
82	packages together. Installed with `npm install -E`.

84	#### 2. Components and pure functions (names per CLAUDE.md §6)
85	
86	| File | Identifier | Role |
87	|---|---|---|
88	| `shared/custom-select.ts` (+ `.html`, `.css`) | `CustomSelect` (`app-custom-select`) | Select-only or searchable combobox, `FormValueControl<string>` |
89	| `shared/date-field.ts` | `DateField` (`app-date-field`) | Date text box + "Elegir fecha" button, `FormValueControl<string>` |
90	| `shared/calendar.ts` | `Calendar` (`app-calendar`) | Dialog content: month label, year list, grid, buttons |
91	| `shared/date-text.ts` | `parseDateText()`, `formatDateText()` | Pure, typed-date grammar of Q-05 |
92	| `shared/calendar-dates.ts` | `monthGrid()`, `nextFocusDate()`, `isDayDisabled()`, `latestValidDate()`, `yearRange()` | Pure, injectable "today" |
93	| `shared/select-search.ts` | `filterOptions()`, `normaliseForSearch()`, `SEARCH_THRESHOLD = 4` | Pure, accent- and case-insensitive contains |
94	
95	#### 3. The custom select
96	
97	- **Focus element.** Select-only (fewer than `SEARCH_THRESHOLD` options): a
98	  `<button type="button" ngCombobox>`; `@angular/aria` treats any non-`input`/`textarea` element as
99	  non-editable (`_combobox-chunk.mjs`: `isEditable` checks the tag), so Enter, Space and ArrowDown
100	  open it and printable keys are relayed to the list for typeahead. Searchable (at or above the
101	  threshold): an `<input type="text" ngCombobox>`; typing expands it and writes the filter text.
102	  Either element gets `id="field-<key>"` (input `controlId`), so the existing `<label for>` targets
103	  it. Its accessible name is the label; for the button variant `aria-labelledby` also points at the
104	  label, so the shown value is not folded into the name in any browser.
105	- **Attributes.** `@angular/aria` binds `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`,
106	  `aria-activedescendant`, `aria-controls`, `aria-haspopup` and `aria-autocomplete` (packed
107	  `fesm2022/combobox.mjs` host bindings). The form binds `aria-required`, `aria-invalid` and
108	  `aria-describedby` through inputs of `CustomSelect` exactly as today (ADR-0004: bound
109	  explicitly), applied to the focus element.
110	- **List.** `<ul ngComboboxWidget ngListbox>` inside `<ng-template ngComboboxPopup>`, with
111	  `focusMode="activedescendant"`, `selectionMode="explicit"`, `[wrap]="false"`; one `ngOption` per
112	  configured option in `sortOrder`, `aria-selected` from the listbox; the selected one shows
113	  `LucideCheck` (hidden) and a style. The prompt "Selecciona una opción" is not an option: it is the
114	  button's text when the value is `''`, and the input's placeholder for a searchable select.
115	- **Behaviour owned by `CustomSelect`** (not provided by `@angular/aria`, each tied to a test row):
116	  Alt+ArrowDown opens on the current option (AC-06); Tab with the list open commits the active
117	  option and lets focus move (AC-06); on a collapsed select-only, a printable key opens and moves to
118	  the first match (AC-06); Escape or leaving a searchable select restores the shown label and clears
119	  the filter without changing the value (AC-07); filtering through `filterOptions()` with the first
120	  match active (Q-11); the result count or the empty text announced politely through the CDK
121	  `LiveAnnouncer` (AC-07, §8.1); a pointer click outside closes without changing the value.
122	- **Panel placement.** A `cdkConnectedOverlay` inside the popup template, anchored to the combobox,
123	  `cdkConnectedOverlayUsePopover="inline"`: in browsers with the Popover API the panel is a native
124	  popover in the top layer, inserted next to the trigger (`@angular/cdk@22.3.0`
125	  `createOverlayRef` defaults `usePopover` to `true` when `showPopover` exists;
126	  `FlexibleOverlayPopoverLocation` `'inline'` inserts it next to the trigger). Below
127	  `--breakpoint-sheet` (`BreakpointObserver` with `(min-width: 37.5em)` false) the same panel uses a
128	  global position strategy anchored to the viewport bottom: full width, at most 85% of the viewport
129	  height, scrollable list, backdrop, option rows of 48 px, and a "Cerrar" button for touch
130	  (`tabindex="-1"`, since focus stays on the combobox and Escape or Tab close it for keyboard users).
131	  Overlays are created with `disableAnimations: true` (ADR-0013).
132	
133	#### 4. The date field and the calendar
134	
135	- **Text box.** `<input type="text" inputmode="numeric" id="field-<key>">`, placeholder
136	  "dd/mm/aaaa", hint "Formato: dd/mm/aaaa" first in `aria-describedby`. No input mask.
137	- **Parsing (pure, `date-text.ts`).** `parseDateText(text)` returns `''` for blank text, the ISO
138	  `YYYY-MM-DD` for `d/m/yyyy` with `/`, `-` or `.` separators (1–2 digit day and month) or exactly
139	  8 digits `ddmmyyyy`, and `null` for anything else, including impossible dates (31/04, 29/02 of a
140	  non-leap year) and 2-digit years (Q-05). `formatDateText(iso)` returns `dd/mm/yyyy`. Every AC-08
141	  row is a unit test. The function lives next to the validators and imports nothing from Angular.
142	- **Binding (`transformedValue`).** `DateField` keeps the shown text with Signal Forms'
143	  `transformedValue(value, { parse, format })` (`@publicApi 22.0`, `@angular/forms@22.3.0`
144	  typings). `parse` returns `{ value: iso }`, `{ value: '' }` for blank, and
145	  `{ value: '', error: { kind: 'parse', message: '' } }` for unreadable text, so the stored value
146	  is `''` and the field is invalid through a `parse` error, which Signal Forms reports to the bound
147	  field automatically and which the existing `errorOf()` already maps to the US-01-AC-09 message
148	  rules (no new message). **Verified hazard:** in `@angular/forms@22.3.0`
149	  (`fesm2022/signals.mjs`, `transformedValue`), the raw value is a `linkedSignal(() =>
150	  format(value()))`, so writing `''` to the model would recompute the shown text to `''` and erase
151	  what the person typed (the R1-F03 failure of US-01 in a new form). Therefore `format(iso)` returns
152	  the last typed text whenever that text parses to `iso` (unreadable text parses to `''`), and
153	  `formatDateText(iso)` otherwise. On blur a readable text is normalised to dd/mm/aaaa. A calendar
154	  choice writes the model, and the text follows through `format`. AC-08's empty-`stored` rows prove
155	  it in a component test.
156	- **"Elegir fecha".** A `<button type="button">` after the text box, accessible name
157	  "Elegir fecha: {label}", `LucideCalendarDays` hidden. It is the one new Tab stop (US-04-BR-13).
158	- **Calendar dialog.** Opened with the CDK `Dialog`: `ariaModal: true`, labelled by the visible
159	  month-and-year text (not a heading, US-04-BR-13), `autoFocus` on the day that holds the roving
160	  `tabindex="0"`, focus returned to "Elegir fecha" on close by passing that button as
161	  `restoreFocus` (the CDK default, `restoreFocus = true`, returns to whatever was focused before
162	  opening, verified in `fesm2022/dialog.mjs`; passing the element also covers browsers where a
163	  pointer click does not focus a button), backdrop, `disableAnimations: true`. The CDK dialog marks the siblings of the overlay container `aria-hidden="true"` while
164	  open (`fesm2022/dialog.mjs`, `_hideNonDialogContentFromAssistiveTechnology`) and traps Tab. Wide
165	  screens: a flexible connected position strategy anchored to the date field; below
166	  `--breakpoint-sheet`: the bottom-sheet strategy of §3.
167	- **Grid.** A `<table role="grid">`, columns Monday first with full day names from
168	  `Intl.DateTimeFormat(<country locale tag>, { weekday: 'long' })`, one `role="gridcell"` per day
169	  with `aria-label` "15 de mayo de 1990" (`{ day, month: 'long', year }`; Node 24 ICU gives exactly
170	  "15 de mayo de 1990" and "mayo de 1990" for es-CO and es-CL), `aria-selected` on the stored day,
171	  `aria-disabled="true"` on disabled days (still reachable with arrows, not choosable). Roving
172	  tabindex. Keys go through the pure `nextFocusDate(date, key, shift)`: arrows ±1 day / ±7 days
173	  crossing months, Home/End to Monday/Sunday of the week, PageUp/PageDown ±1 month clamped to the
174	  month's last day, Shift+PageUp/PageDown ±1 year clamped (29/02/2000 → 28/02/2001), Enter/Space
175	  choose, Escape closes. `@angular/aria`'s `ngGrid` is not used: it moves only inside the rendered
176	  rows (arrows, Home/End, Ctrl+Home/End in `_widget-chunk.mjs`) and has no PageUp/PageDown, so the
177	  calendar would override most keys anyway.
178	- **Year list.** "Elegir año" swaps the grid for an `ngListbox` (`focusMode="roving"`,
179	  `selectionMode="explicit"`, `[wrap]="false"`) of the years of `yearRange()`, the current year
180	  selected; Enter chooses, returns to the grid on the same day and month of the chosen year (clamped).
181	- **Disabled days and range (D6).** `isDayDisabled(config, iso, today)` is
182	  `validateField(config, iso, today) !== null` (the value is never empty, so "required" never
183	  applies). `latestValidDate()` probes backwards from today with the same function;
184	  `yearRange()` is [Y−120, year of the latest valid date] when the field has any rule that
185	  disables days, else [Y−120, Y+10] (Q-12). No `minAge` arithmetic is written twice.
186	
187	#### 5. Signal Forms integration (D3)
188	
189	- `CustomSelect` and `DateField` implement `FormValueControl<string>` (`@publicApi 22.0`): a
190	  required `value = model<string>()`, a `touch` output emitted when focus leaves the whole widget
191	  (control, button, panel), and a `focus()` method that focuses the labelled element. The form
192	  template binds them with the existing narrowing accessor `[formField]="text(config.key)"`; no new
193	  cast (ADR-0004's "two accessors are the only casts" holds).
194	- `focusBoundControl()` calls the control's `focus()` when it is implemented (typings of
195	  `FormUiControl.focus`: "If the focus method is not implemented, Signal Forms will attempt to focus
196	  the host element"), so a failed "Continuar" focuses the combobox or the date text box (AC-10 of
197	  US-01, unchanged).
198	- The components declare **no** inputs named `invalid`, `required`, `touched`, `errors` or
199	  `disabled`: `FormField` auto-binds inputs with those names (`FormUiControl`), which would show
200	  `aria-invalid` before the field is touched. The form passes the shown-error state explicitly.
201	- Stored values: option `value`, ISO date or `''`, as before (ADR-0003, ADR-0004).
202	
203	#### 6. Store writer (amends the ADR-0004 implementation note)
204	
205	`date` keys leave the `nativeKeys` set of `quote-form.ts`: the date model now holds `''` for
206	unreadable text, so the model is the truth and `flushModel()` writes date keys like text and select
207	keys. `syncNative` and `validity.badInput` remain for `number` only.
208	
209	#### 7. Lazy step 1 (D8)
210	
211	Measured on a throwaway copy of `frontend/` (production build, `@angular/build` 22.3.0; baseline
212	initial `main` 381.44 kB raw / 98.94 kB transfer): `@angular/aria` combobox and listbox with CDK
213	overlay, dialog, a11y and layout **+125.40 kB raw / +27.81 kB transfer**; CDK alone **+99.29 /
214	+22.58**. With the icons of ADR-0010, an eager build would pass the 500 kB warning. The
215	`/:country/datos` route therefore uses `loadComponent` for `QuoteFormPage`, so these packages and
216	the step 1 icons load in a lazy chunk. The address, the guards and the "focus the arriving `h1`"
217	rule of ADR-0001 are unchanged; the existing static guard forbids lazy loading only in the summary
218	feature (US-03-AC-03). The budgets of `angular.json` are not changed.
219	
220	#### 8. What tests can and cannot see
221	
222	- **Component tests (jsdom 31.0.1).** jsdom has no `showPopover` and no `inert` (checked in the
223	  installed package), so the CDK falls back to its overlay container under `document.body`: panels
224	  and the calendar render **outside** the component's root. Helpers find them through the
225	  combobox's `aria-controls` (once rendered) or by role in `document`, as spec §11.1 already plans.
226	  The overlay container is torn down between tests.
227	- **E2E (Playwright).** Page-wide role queries are unaffected by where the panel sits. Focus trap,
228	  real key sequences, bottom-sheet geometry and the 44 px boxes are proven here.
229	
230	### Consequences
231	
232	- Good, because the APG combobox wiring comes from a maintained Angular package, not from our code
233	  (D1, D2), and the date logic that is ours is pure and unit-tested row by row.
234	- Good, because the labelled element stays a native `<input>` or `<button>`: `<label for>`,
235	  `label.control`, `getByLabel` and the `aria-*` bindings keep working (D4); §11.1's changes stay
236	  by role and label.
237	- Good, because validation, messages, stored values and the submit focus rule do not change
238	  (D3): `validateField` is still the only rule engine, now also deciding disabled days (D6).
239	- Good, because the bundle stays within budget by moving step 1 to a lazy chunk (D8).
240	- Bad, because `@angular/aria` has been stable only since 22.0.0 (2026-06-03, about five and a half
241	  months) and its combobox was rewritten in that release (legacy combobox removed,
242	  `SimpleCombobox` promoted to `Combobox`, `values` renamed `value`) — mitigation: pinned 22.3.0;
243	  the use is confined to `CustomSelect` and the year list; every keyboard row is a test.
244	- Bad, because `@angular/aria` renders the popup lazily, so `aria-controls` is absent while the
245	  combobox is collapsed, at least until the list has been opened once (host binding `[attr.aria-controls]: _pattern.popupId()`, and the popup
246	  widget registers only when rendered), while WAI-ARIA 1.2 says authors "MUST set aria-controls on a
247	  combobox element to a value that refers to the combobox popup element" — mitigation: the gap is
248	  reported to the spec (*Spec impact* 3) and checked with a screen reader at HC3. `preserveContent`
249	  (an inherited input of `Combobox`) keeps the popup template rendered after the first open, but
250	  the listbox sits inside the CDK overlay's own template, which is detached on close, so the
251	  developer must confirm in a component test whether the reference survives a close; if the human
252	  requires strict conformance, option B can replace `@angular/aria` inside `CustomSelect` without
253	  touching the form.
254	- Bad, because the wrapper still owns several behaviours (Alt+ArrowDown, Tab commit, collapsed
255	  typeahead, Escape restore, filtering, announcements, sheet) — mitigation: each maps to an AC-06/07
256	  row and is tested in both select kinds.
257	- Bad, because the date text needs a custom `format` to keep unreadable text visible (verified
258	  `linkedSignal` hazard) — mitigation: AC-08 rows with an empty `stored` value test exactly this.
259	- Bad, because jsdom cannot show the top layer, `inert` or real focus trapping — mitigation: e2e.
260	- Neutral: two packages of about 3.6 MB (`@angular/cdk`) and 1.2 MB (`@angular/aria`) unpacked in
261	  `node_modules`; only what is imported reaches the bundle.
262	
263	### Strongest argument against
264	
265	Option B (CDK only) builds on the most proven parts of the Angular ecosystem:
266	`ActiveDescendantKeyManager`, `Overlay` and `Dialog` have years of production use, while
267	`@angular/aria` has been stable for under six months, had its combobox rewritten with breaking
268	changes in 22.0.0, has had about two dozen fixes since, leaves `aria-controls` off a collapsed
269	combobox, has no date picker at all, and adds 26 kB raw on top of the CDK. With B every
270	ARIA attribute is ours to set exactly as the APG says, so the `aria-controls` gap does not exist,
271	and there is one primitive library to understand instead of two.
272	
273	**Why we accept it:** under B the combobox's role, states, key relay, typeahead hand-off and
274	close-on-focus-out are hand-written: that is the "from scratch" part the story rules out, and the
275	part where accessibility bugs usually live. `@angular/aria` is the Angular team's implementation of
276	exactly that pattern, its developer-preview tag was removed in 22.0.0, and it peer-pins the same CDK
277	we need anyway. The decision is contained: `@angular/aria` is used only inside `CustomSelect` and
278	the year list, both behind `FormValueControl<string>`, so falling back to B later rewrites one
279	component, not the form. The 26 kB are in a lazy chunk.

300	## Pros and Cons of the Options
301	
302	### A. `@angular/aria` + `@angular/cdk` (chosen)
303	
304	- Good, because the combobox and listbox follow the APG pattern with library-maintained ARIA and
305	  keyboard wiring; works on `<input>` and `<button>`.
306	- Good, because the CDK covers positioning, popover top layer, bottom sheet, modal focus trap and
307	  return, `aria-hidden` of the page behind, and announcements.
308	- Bad, because the library is young (stable since 22.0.0) and has gaps the wrapper fills.
309	- Bad, because +125.40 kB raw for both packages (measured), hence the lazy step 1.
310	
311	### B. `@angular/cdk` only
312	
313	- Good, because every primitive is long-established; one library; full control of every attribute.
314	- Good, because +99.29 kB raw (measured), 26 kB less than A.
315	- Bad, because the combobox ARIA wiring and key handling are hand-written around the key manager:
316	  more custom accessibility code to get right and to test (story: "not from scratch").
317	- Bad, because `cdk/listbox` expects focus inside the listbox, which does not fit a combobox whose

8	
9	# ADR-0013: Motion with native `animate.enter` and CSS on duration tokens, enter-only step transition, reduced motion by construction
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	US-04 asks for an animated step indicator, a transition between steps, hover, focus, active and
14	disabled states, soft validation feedback, skeletons while Strapi loads, interactive plan cards
15	and summary micro-animations, all honouring `prefers-reduced-motion` ("no movement if the user asks
16	for it"), and asks the ADR to propose the library and "justify bundle weight and maintenance"
17	(story; US-04-BR-09, BR-10). The step transition must not put two pages, two `main` or two `h1`
18	elements in the document at once, and focus must still land on the arriving `h1` (US-04-AC-14;
19	ADR-0001). This ADR picks the mechanism, the motion tokens, the step transition and how reduced
20	motion is applied and tested (US-04-Q-14, Q-16).
21	
22	## Decision Drivers
23	
24	- D1. No movement under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`: every computed animation and transition
25	  duration 0 s and no running animation (US-04-BR-10, AC-17).
26	- D2. One page in the DOM during a step change, focus on the arriving `h1`, document title as today
27	  (US-04-AC-14; ADR-0001 "Focus on step change"; ADR-0009 heading outline).
28	- D3. Bundle weight and maintenance justified (story); budgets kept (spec §9); exact versions and a
29	  permissive licence for anything new (US-04-BR-14).
30	- D4. Animate `transform` and `opacity` only (spec §9, Performance).
31	- D5. Durations and easings are tokens (US-04-BR-01, ADR-0010).
32	- D6. Motion never interferes with announcements: role `alert`/`status` text is in the DOM at once
33	  (spec §8; US-04-Q-16: no counting-up of numbers).
34	- D7. Restraint: motion answers a person's action; one orchestrated moment beats scattered effects
35	  (vendored `frontend-design` skill, adopted with CLAUDE.md §5 overrides).
36	
37	## Considered Options
38	
39	1. **A. Native `animate.enter` / `animate.leave` + CSS keyframes and transitions** on duration and
40	   easing tokens; no animation library.
41	2. **B. Router `withViewTransitions()`** (View Transitions API) for the step change, plus CSS for
42	   everything else.
43	3. **C. An animation library**: Motion (`motion` 14.14.0) or GSAP (`gsap` 3.15.1), driven from
44	   `(animate.enter)` / `(animate.leave)` callbacks.
45	
46	## Decision Outcome
47	
48	Chosen option: **"A. Native `animate.enter` + CSS on tokens"**, because it costs zero bytes and no
49	dependency (D3), is stable public API in 22.3.0, covers every effect the spec lists with
50	`transform` and `opacity` (D4), and lets reduced motion be guaranteed by construction rather than by
51	overrides (D1). An enter-only page animation keeps exactly one page in the DOM (D2). B covers only
52	route changes, so it would be a second mechanism next to A, and it became public API only in this
53	very version. C adds 71–74 kB raw per library for effects CSS already does, and GSAP's licence is
54	not an OSI licence.
55	
56	### What is decided
57	
58	#### 1. Motion tokens (in `tokens.css`, ADR-0010)
59	
60	| Token | Value | Used for |
61	|---|---|---|
62	| `--duration-fast` | 120ms | hover, press, focus ring, error fade-in, panel close (exits are faster than entries) |
63	| `--duration-base` | 200ms | step enter, panel open, bottom-sheet slide, indicator fill, segmented control |
64	| `--duration-slow` | 320ms | confirmation check-circle; upper bound of any single transition (AC-14) |
65	| `--delay-stagger-1` … `--delay-stagger-4` | 0ms, 50ms, 100ms, 150ms | summary sections (total ≤ 150 + 200 = 350 ms, under Q-16's 400 ms) |
66	| `--duration-shimmer` | 1400ms | skeleton shimmer loop |
67	| `--duration-spin` | 800ms | "Pagar" processing spinner |
68	| `--ease-out` | `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` | entries |
69	| `--ease-in` | `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)` | exits |
70	| `--ease-standard` | `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` | state changes (colour, border, glow) |
71	| `--motion-rise` | 0.5rem (8 px) | step enter and panel offset |
72	
73	No bounce or overshoot curves. Under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` every `--duration-*`
74	and `--delay-*` token is `0ms` (a second line of defence; see §3).
75	
76	#### 2. Where motion is used (and where it is not)
77	
78	| Effect | Mechanism | Property |
79	|---|---|---|
80	| Step change | `animate.enter="page-enter"` on the root element of each routed page; **no** `animate.leave` | opacity 0 → 1, translateY(`--motion-rise`) → 0, `--duration-base`, `--ease-out` |
81	| Step indicator fill | CSS transition on the progress bar | `transform: scaleX()` |
82	| Select panel open | `animate.enter` on the panel | opacity, translateY(−`--motion-rise`/2) |
83	| Bottom sheet open | `animate.enter` on the sheet | translateY(100%) → 0 |
84	| Panel close | instant by default; `animate.leave` only if the developer confirms it runs when the CDK overlay detaches (no AC needs it) | opacity |
85	| Error text | `animate.enter="error-enter"` | opacity only (no shake); the text is in the DOM, inside `role="alert"`, from the first frame (D6) |
86	| Hover / active / chosen plan | CSS transitions | `border-color`, `box-shadow`, `background-color` (paint), and a 2 px lift on hover only for `(hover: hover)` pointers |
87	| Skeleton shimmer | keyframes on a pseudo-element | `transform: translateX()` |
88	| "Pagar" spinner | keyframes on the icon | `transform: rotate()` |
89	| Summary sections | `animate.enter` with `--delay-stagger-n` by `:nth-of-type` | opacity, translateY |
90	| Confirmation | `animate.enter` on the check-circle | scale 0.85 → 1 and opacity, `--duration-slow` (the single orchestrated moment of the flow) |
91	
92	Not animated: prices and numbers (no counting up, D6), headings, the country chooser list, text in
93	live regions. Hover transitions are colour and shadow changes, not motion, except the 2 px lift
94	(D7: "hover transitions on every card" read as generated; the plan cards are the one place where a
95	lift explains "this is clickable", US-04-BR-09).
96	
97	**Step transition, why one page only.** The router removes the leaving component and inserts the
98	arriving one in the same change; with no `animate.leave`, Angular does not keep the old element.
99	Only the arriving page animates in, so there is never a second `h1` or `main` (AC-14). Focus moves
100	to the arriving `h1` as today: opacity and transform do not affect focus or the accessibility tree.
101	
102	#### 3. Reduced motion, by construction (D1)
103	
104	- In every style file except `tokens.css`, each `animation`, `animation-*`, `transition` and
105	  `transition-*` declaration sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { … }`.
106	  Under `reduce` no animation or transition is declared at all: computed durations are the initial
107	  `0s`, `document.getAnimations()` is empty, and states (colour, border, icon, text) still change,
108	  instantly. This keeps feedback while removing movement, a principle restated from
109	  `pbakaus/impeccable` `animate.md` (Apache-2.0, credited per EVAL-004), and it avoids the global
110	  `0.01ms !important` kill switch that the same source flags.
111	- `animate.enter` classes therefore have no animation under `reduce`; Angular reads the computed
112	  styles, finds none, and removes the class at once (`@angular/core@22.3.0`
113	  `determineLongestAnimation` falls back to computed styles when `getAnimations()` is empty;
114	  `MAX_ANIMATION_TIMEOUT` default 4000 ms is never reached).
115	- The duration tokens are also set to `0ms` under `reduce` in `tokens.css`, so a declaration that
116	  escapes the `no-preference` block still has no duration.
117	- **CDK overlays and dialogs** (ADR-0012) are created with `disableAnimations: true`. The CDK's own
118	  backdrop has `transition: opacity 400ms` and, under reduced motion, `transition-duration: 1ms`
119	  (`@angular/cdk@22.3.0` overlay styles), which would fail AC-17's "0s"; with
120	  `disableAnimations`, the CDK adds `cdk-overlay-backdrop-noop-animation` (`transition: none`). Our
121	  own backdrop fade, if any, is a token transition inside the `no-preference` block in
122	  `styles.css`.
123	- The spinner stops under `reduce`; "Procesando pago…" (US-03) remains the feedback.
124	
125	#### 4. Tests (AC-14, AC-17)
126	
127	- **Static guard** (extends ADR-0010's guard): outside `tokens.css`, no `animation`/`transition`
128	  declaration outside a `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` block; durations, delays and
129	  easings only as `var(--duration-*)`, `var(--delay-*)`, `var(--ease-*)`; `tokens.css` sets every
130	  `--duration-*` and `--delay-*` to `0ms` under `reduce`; every `createOverlayRef`,
131	  `cdkConnectedOverlay` and `Dialog.open` call passes `disableAnimations: true` (a grep on the
132	  production sources).
133	- **E2E AC-17**: a Playwright context with `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` walks step 1 (with "Ciudad"
134	  open and the calendar open), step 2, the summary and the confirmation; on each state it asserts
135	  that every element's computed `animationDuration` and `transitionDuration` list only `0s`, and
136	  `document.getAnimations()` is empty.
137	- **E2E AC-14**: with motion allowed, a `MutationObserver` installed before "Continuar" records the
138	  maximum number of `h1` and `main` elements seen during navigation (expected 1 and 1); then focus
139	  is on "Elige tu plan" and the title is unchanged; the page's enter animation reports a duration
140	  ≤ `--duration-slow` through `getAnimations()`.
141	
142	### Consequences
143	
144	- Good, because no dependency, no bytes, no licence question (D3); `animate.enter` is
145	  `@publicApi 20.2` in `@angular/core@22.3.0` and the vendored skill's own guidance for v20.2+.
146	- Good, because reduced motion is a property of how styles are written, enforced by a guard, not a
147	  late override that can be missed (D1).
148	- Good, because one page is ever in the DOM (D2), and focus and announcements are untouched (D6).
149	- Bad, because the old page disappears without an exit animation, so the change is a cut followed by
150	  a fade-in, less fluid than a cross-fade — mitigation: the fade is short (200 ms) and the step
151	  indicator fill gives continuity; B can be added later as an enhancement if the human wants a
152	  cross-fade (see *Revisit*).
153	- Bad, because closing a panel inside a CDK overlay may not run `animate.leave` (the overlay detaches
154	  its content) — mitigation: panels close instantly unless the developer proves the leave runs; no
155	  AC requires a close animation.
156	- Bad, because writing every animation inside a media block is a discipline — mitigation: the guard
157	  fails the gate otherwise.
158	- Neutral: the first page load also plays `page-enter` once; that is the single page-load moment.
159	
160	### Strongest argument against
161	
162	The View Transitions route (B) gives a real two-state transition with one line,
163	`withViewTransitions()`: the browser snapshots the old page and cross-fades it into the new one,
164	while the live DOM still holds only the new page (so AC-14 holds too). It can even morph the step
165	indicator between steps with a `view-transition-name`, which is the "animated step indicator" the
166	story asks for, and browsers without support simply skip it. Enter-only CSS is a hard cut followed
167	by a fade, the kind of generic "fade-and-rise" the `frontend-design` skill calls a tell of generated
168	pages.
169	
170	**Why we accept it:** B only animates route changes, so the panels, errors, skeletons, cards,
171	spinner and confirmation still need A: two mechanisms, two reduced-motion paths (B also needs
172	`skipTransition()` or `::view-transition-*` rules under `reduce`, and its pseudo-element
173	animations show up in `document.getAnimations()` during AC-17). `withViewTransitions` is tagged
174	`@publicApi 22.3` in the 22.3.0 typings, so it has been public API only since the release we pin,
175	three days before this ADR. The fade-in here is brief and paired with the indicator fill, and the
176	one orchestrated moment is the confirmation, as the skill advises. B stays a contained later
177	enhancement on top of A.
178	
179	### Confirmation
180	
181	- Static guard rules of §4 (US-04-AC-17, AC-01).
182	- E2E `us-04-design-system.spec.ts`: AC-14 and AC-17 as in §4.
183	- Component tests (AC-15): skeletons are `aria-hidden`, the loading text stays in its live region.
184	- HC3: the human checks the motion with the OS setting on and off (AC-23).
185	- `frontend/package.json` contains no `motion`, `gsap`, `@angular/animations` or other animation
186	  dependency (dependency list guard of ADR-0010).
187	
188	## Pros and Cons of the Options
189	
190	### A. Native `animate.enter` / `animate.leave` + CSS (chosen)
191	
192	- Good, because zero bytes and zero dependencies; stable API since 20.2.
193	- Good, because every effect is plain CSS on tokens, and reduced motion is enforced statically.
194	- Bad, because there is no exit for the leaving page (by design) and limited choreography.
195	
196	### B. Router `withViewTransitions()`
197	
198	`@angular/router@22.3.0` typings: `withViewTransitions` tagged `@publicApi 22.3`.
199	
200	- Good, because a true cross-fade (or a morph of named elements) with one line; one page in the DOM.
201	- Good, because progressive: unsupported browsers navigate without a transition.
202	- Bad, because it covers route changes only; everything else still needs A.
203	- Bad, because reduced motion needs its own handling, and its animations appear in
204	  `document.getAnimations()` while running.
205	- Bad, because it became public API in 22.3.0 itself.
206	
207	### C. Motion 14.14.0 or GSAP 3.15.1
208	
209	Verified on npm (2026-11-21): `motion@14.14.0` MIT, unpacked 1.0 MB; `gsap@3.15.1` licence
210	"Standard 'no charge' license: https://gsap.com/standard-license", unpacked 6.3 MB. Measured on a
211	throwaway build (baseline initial 381.44 kB raw / 98.94 kB transfer): `import { animate } from
212	'motion'` **+74.10 kB raw / +23.97 kB transfer**; `motion/mini` **+8.92 / +2.71**; `gsap`
213	**+71.36 / +25.00**.
214	
215	- Good, because springs, timelines and sequencing beyond CSS.
216	- Bad, because nothing in the spec needs them: every listed effect is a CSS transform or opacity.
217	- Bad, because the weight is real (motion, gsap) or the features are what CSS already has
218	  (motion/mini); one more dependency to upgrade.
219	- Bad, because GSAP's licence is not an OSI permissive licence, so US-04-BR-14 would need a human
220	  exception.
221

229	3. **US-04-AC-17** "document.getAnimations() returns no running animation": with §3 it returns no

The first day of the week (grid column order and the week bounds of Home/End) follows the country's locale (`localeTag`) from CLDR week data: Sunday for es-CO, Monday for es-CL. It is derived from the locale at runtime, with no country code or per-country table in the date picker (human decision at HC1, 2026-11-21).

lines: | US-04-BR-03 | "Flags of Colombia and Chile in SVG (a licensed library or our own optimized SVGs), visible in the country selector/context and in the wizard header. A per-country accent color through tokens. The flag is decorative next to the country name (`aria-hidden`), never the only indicator." | The country chooser links and the wizard header show the flag SVG of the country next to its Strapi `name`. The flag is `aria-hidden="true"`, has no text content and is not focusable; the link's accessible name stays the country name ("Colombia", "Chile"). The country accent token takes the current country's value on the wizard pages; a published country with no flag or accent in the front end shows a neutral globe icon and the brand accent (US-04-Q-02). Mechanism: the presentation-only map `frontend/src/app/shared/country-visuals.ts` keyed by ISO code, returning a flag component and an accent key, never a colour (ADR-0011, which amends ADR-0001). Quoted country codes appear in production `.ts`/`.html` only in that file, and `data-country-accent` selectors only in `tokens.css`; a static guard enforces it, replacing ADR-0001's review grep (ADR-0011 *Confirmation*). No behaviour, validation, routing, guard, price, copy or request reads the map. | US-04-AC-03 |

| US-04-BR-04 | "Icons: a single library with SVG icons imported individually … inside the inputs (document, name, date, city, plate, make, model, year), in the wizard steps, in the plans, in help, error and success messages. The input icon comes from a front-end mapping by field key, with a generic default icon for new fields … Decorative icons `aria-hidden`; icons that carry meaning have a label." | One icon library, icons imported one by one (no full-set import, no icon font, no runtime fetch): `@lucide/angular` 1.77.0, ISC (US-04-Q-09, ADR-0010 §7). Step 1: every `text`, `number`, `select` and `date` field shows the icon mapped from its `key` (§7.2), or the default icon for any other key; `checkbox` fields show none. Icons in steps, plan lists (check-circle), help, error and success messages. Every icon that sits next to text saying the same thing is decorative: `aria-hidden="true"`, not focusable, no `<title>` and no text content, so no accessible name or `textContent` of a control changes. An icon without adjacent text (an icon-only button) has an accessible name from §8.1. | US-04-AC-04, US-04-AC-20 |

| US-04-BR-05 | "Select: our own dropdown in the design system's style, with an icon, search when the list is long (e.g. cities, makes), and the selected option marked." "Built on accessible primitives, not from scratch … Full accessibility per the WAI-ARIA patterns (combobox/listbox …): arrows, Enter, Escape, Home/End … screen-reader announcements." | Every `select` field renders a custom select following the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with a listbox popup (select-only below the search threshold, editable with list filtering at or above it, US-04-Q-11). The element that takes focus is the element the field's `<label for>` points at (a `<button>` for a select-only, an `<input type="text">` for a searchable select, ADR-0012 §3, so `label.control`, `getByLabel` and `labels[0]` keep working) and carries `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-required`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` as the native control did, plus `aria-controls` referring to the listbox **while the list is rendered** (`@angular/aria` omits it while collapsed, at least before the first open; ADR-0012 *Consequences*; checked with a screen reader at HC3). Empty, the prompt "Selecciona una opción" is its shown value: the button's text for a select-only, the placeholder for a searchable select (whose input value is then `''`). The prompt is not an option (supersedes the "first entry is a non-selectable prompt" wording of US-01-BR-02, US-04-Q-04). The listbox contains exactly the configured options in `sortOrder`; the selected option is marked visually (check icon + style) and with `aria-selected="true"`. Choosing an option stores its `value` (unchanged). Keyboard per US-04-AC-06; built on `@angular/aria` 22.3.0 and `@angular/cdk` 22.3.0 (US-04-Q-04, ADR-0012). | US-04-AC-05, US-04-AC-06, US-04-AC-07, US-04-AC-12 |

-| US-04-BR-06 | "Calendar (birth date): our own date picker with month navigation and fast year navigation (a year selector …), days disabled according to the rules (minAge), and the date can also be typed by hand." Same accessibility clause as BR-05: "date picker dialog … focus trapped and returned on close". | Every `date` field renders a text box (the labelled control) and an "Elegir fecha" button that opens the calendar (WAI-ARIA date picker dialog). Typed entry: format dd/mm/aaaa for every country, independent of the browser locale, parsed and stored as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` (US-04-Q-05). Text that is not a complete, existing date is treated exactly like the former `validity.badInput` (US-01-BR-01, US-01-AC-09 note): stored `''`, text kept visible, field invalid whether required or optional, same message resolution. Calendar: month navigation, year selector, keyboard per US-04-AC-09, focus trapped while open and returned to "Elegir fecha" on close. A day is disabled if and only if the shared validator of the field (the same pure function used for validation, no second implementation) rejects that date for a reason other than "required" (with the seed's `minAge` 18: every day after the 18th anniversary limit and every future day). Disabled days can still be typed; typing one shows the configured message (validation unchanged). | US-04-AC-08, US-04-AC-09, US-04-AC-10, US-04-AC-12 |

| US-04-BR-07 | "Validations and the stored value do not change." "Logic, the contracts with Strapi and the texts that come from Strapi do not change; it is a visual change. The existing e2e tests must keep passing without being loosened; if a selector changes, it is adjusted using accessible roles/labels, not CSS classes." | For the same user input, the editing model, the `quote-wizard` entry, the typed step 1 output, the error shown, the focus target on a failed "Continuar", the routes, the prices, the summary and the payment behave exactly as before US-04. No file under `backend/` changes. Every existing unit, component and e2e test passes; a test changes only as listed in §11.1, where each change keeps or raises the assertion's strength and finds elements by role, label or visible text (never by class or id). | US-04-AC-11 |

| US-04-BR-08 | "Supporting text: clear microcopy in help texts, placeholders, empty states and errors … Business content keeps coming from Strapi; only interface texts live in the front end." | Front-end copy added by US-04 is exactly §8.1 (Spanish, same for both countries). Existing code-owned strings (US-01..US-03 §8.1) and every Strapi text stay unchanged (US-04-Q-07). Day and month names come from `Intl` with the country's `localeTag`, not from literals. | US-04-AC-07, US-04-AC-09, US-04-AC-11, US-04-AC-13 |

| US-04-BR-09 | "Interactions and animation: an animated wizard step indicator, transition between steps, hover/focus/active/disabled states, validation with soft feedback, skeletons while Strapi loads, plan selection with interactive cards, and a summary with micro-animations." | Step indicator per US-04-Q-17 (not focusable, current step exposed with `aria-current="step"`). Step change: enter-only transition of the arriving page (no two pages in the DOM at once), focus on the arriving `h1` as today (US-04-Q-14). Every interactive control has distinct hover, focus-visible, active and disabled (including `aria-disabled`) styles. Soft feedback: an error appears with a short fade and its icon, no shaking, no colour-only signal. Skeletons replace the loading text visually on step 1, step 2, the terms region and the country list, while the existing loading text stays in its live region (US-04-Q-15). Plan cards: a pointer click anywhere on a card chooses its plan; the native radio stays the keyboard and accessibility control. Summary and confirmation micro-animations per US-04-Q-16. Library per the motion ADR. | US-04-AC-13, US-04-AC-14, US-04-AC-15, US-04-AC-16, US-04-AC-23 |

toolUseResult.newString: Summary and confirmation micro-animations per US-04-Q-16. Mechanism: Angular native `animate.enter` and CSS on the duration and easing tokens, no animation library, no `animate.leave` on pages (ADR-0013). Movement uses `transform` and `opacity` only; state changes may transition paint-only properties (colours, border colour, shadow); the 2 px card lift on hover applies only under `(hover: hover)`. |

toolUseResult.newString: | With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, every CSS animation and transition and every Angular enter/leave animation has a computed duration of 0 s (or none), `document.getAnimations()` is empty, and no element changes position, size or rotation over time (skeleton shimmer, step transition, panel slide, indicator fill, spinner, micro-animations all off). States still change instantly. By construction (ADR-0013 §3): outside `tokens.css` every `animation*`/`transition*` declaration sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`; `tokens.css` sets every `--duration-*` and `--delay-*` to `0ms` under `reduce`; every CDK overlay and dialog is created with `disableAnimations: true`. A static guard checks the three. |

It is derived from the locale at runtime, with no country code or per-country table in the date picker (human decision at HC1, 2026-11-21).

input.new_string: Summary and confirmation micro-animations per US-04-Q-16. Mechanism: Angular native `animate.enter` and CSS on the duration and easing tokens, no animation library, no `animate.leave` on pages (ADR-0013). input.old_string: | With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, every CSS animation and transition and every Angular enter/leave animation has a computed duration of 0 s (or none), and no element changes position, size or rotation over time (skeleton shimmer, step transition, panel slide, indicator fill, micro-animations all off). States still change instantly. |
input.new_string: | With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, every CSS animation and transition and every Angular enter/leave animation has a computed duration of 0 s (or none), `document.getAnimations()` is empty, and no element changes position, size or rotation over time (skeleton shimmer, step transition, panel slide, indicator fill, spinner, micro-animations all off). By construction (ADR-0013 §3): outside `tokens.css` every `animation*`/`transition*` declaration sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`; `tokens.css` sets every `--duration-*` and `--delay-*` to `0ms` under `reduce`; every CDK overlay and dialog is created with `disableAnimations: true`. A static guard checks the three. |

    | Chile    | 15/05/1990  | PageDown        | 15/06/1990 |

    | Chile    | 15/05/1990  | Escape          | the dialog closes, the field value is unchanged, focus on "Elegir fecha" |

Scenario: Focus stays in the calendar
  Given the calendar is open
  When I press Tab repeatedly, or Shift+Tab repeatedly
  Then the focus cycles through "Elegir año", "Mes anterior", "Mes siguiente", the grid and "Cerrar" only
  And a backdrop covers the page behind, so a pointer click there does not reach the page
  And the page content behind the dialog is hidden from assistive technology (aria-hidden="true" on the siblings of the overlay container)

Scenario Outline: Calendar names and first day of the week
  Given the calendar is open in <country> on May 1990
  Then the grid's column headers expose the full Spanish day names in the order <order>
  And each day cell's accessible name is the full date, for example "15 de mayo de 1990"
  And the selected day has aria-selected="true"

  Examples:
    | country  | order |
    | Colombia | "domingo", "lunes", "martes", "miércoles", "jueves", "viernes", "sábado" |
    | Chile    | "lunes", "martes", "miércoles", "jueves", "viernes", "sábado", "domingo" |
```

15/05/1990 is a Tuesday. The first day of the week comes from the country `localeTag` and CLDR
week data (BR-06; human decision at HC1), not from a country code: the unit test of the grid and
of `nextFocusDate` takes the locale tag as input, and Home/End move to the first and last day of
that locale's week. The CDK dialog does not set the HTML `inert` attribute (ADR-0012 §4); the
focus trap, the backdrop and `aria-hidden` are asserted instead, the focus trap and the backdrop
in e2e (jsdom has no real focus trapping), `aria-hidden` in the component test.

And the transition lasts at most the "slow" duration token
```

The transition is enter-only (`animate.enter` on the arriving page, no `animate.leave`), so the
leaving page is removed at once (ADR-0013 §2). The "slow" token is `--duration-slow` (320 ms); the
page enter uses `--duration-base` (200 ms). A `MutationObserver` installed before "Continuar"
records the maximum `h1` and `main` counts (ADR-0013 §4).

input.old_string:
Then at every page and with every panel open, every element's computed animation-duration and transition-duration are 0s
  And document.getAnimations() returns no running animation
```
input.new_string:
Then at every page and with every panel open, every element's computed animation-duration and transition-duration are 0s
  And document.getAnimations() returns an empty list

Scenario: Reduced motion by construction
  Given the production style files and sources of frontend/src
  Then outside tokens.css every animation and transition declaration is inside a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) block
  And tokens.css sets every --duration-* and --delay-* token to 0ms under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  And every CDK overlay and dialog is created with disableAnimations: true
```

The second scenario is the static guard of ADR-0013 §4. `disableAnimations` matters because the
CDK backdrop otherwise keeps a 1 ms transition under reduced motion (ADR-0013 §3).

input.old_string:

  And every font request is a WOFF2 file of at most two families
  And the production styles declare at most two font families plus a generic fallback
```

Then every request the browser sends goes to the app's own origin
  And every font request is a WOFF2 file under /fonts/, at most one file per family and at most two families
  And the production styles declare at most two @font-face families, each with one WOFF2 src on the app origin, font-display: swap and a font-weight range
  And any other family name in a font-family declaration is a local system fallback that is never requested
```

With variable fonts each family is one file covering a weight range (BR-12, ADR-0010 §5); the
static guard counts `@font-face` families, and the e2e counts font requests.

input.old_string:

  And each addition is listed in its ADR with exact version and license
```

And the dependency names are exactly the pre-US-04 list plus the additions accepted in the US-04 ADRs
  And each addition is listed in its ADR with exact version and license
```

| US-04-Q-04 | **[Blocks HC1] [ADR]** Custom select and date picker: which accessible primitives (Angular CDK Overlay/Listbox/A11y vs `@angular/aria` at 22.3.0), and how they bind to Signal Forms and the shared validation core (ADR-0004) without changing validation or stored values. This also **supersedes** three approved US-01 decisions: Q-22 ("Native `<input type=\"date\">`"), §9 ("Native controls are used … `select`") and the BR-02 wording "the first entry is a non-selectable prompt" (the prompt becomes the empty shown value, not an option). | The story requires custom controls; ADR-0004 decided Signal Forms with native controls in mind (`syncNative`, `badInput`, `focusBoundControl`). The test changes of §11.1 depend on the element chosen. | Decided by an ADR (§10). Constraints the spec sets: the focusable element is labelable (`<input>` or `<button>`) and targeted by the field's `<label for>`; it is the control `focusBoundControl()` focuses; the model keeps strings (option value, ISO date, `''`); validation stays in `field-validators.ts`; for the date, unreadable text maps to `''` with the same message rules (BR-06), replacing the `syncNative` path for dates only. The three supersessions are consistent with it (ADR-0012 *Spec impact* 6). | OK as proposed. — Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21 (HC1) |

| US-04-Q-05 | **[Blocks HC1]** Date typed entry: format, accepted variants, how it maps to ISO, and what an incomplete or impossible date does. | Changes the US-01-AC-24 keyboard path (today: segments typed in the browser locale) and the R3-F01 tests; must keep the `badInput` semantics. | dd/mm/aaaa for every country, independent of browser locale; accepted: `d/m/yyyy` with `/`, `-` or `.` separators (1–2 digit day and month), or exactly 8 digits `ddmmyyyy`; 4-digit year only. Re-displayed as dd/mm/aaaa on leaving the field. Incomplete, impossible (31/04, 29/02 of a non-leap year) or 2-digit-year text → stored `''`, text kept, invalid with the existing message rules (no new validation message; a more specific "Ingresa una fecha válida (dd/mm/aaaa)." would be a validation-copy change and is not proposed). Placeholder and hint "dd/mm/aaaa" are code-owned (§8.1); the hint is part of the accessible description. No input mask that inserts characters while typing. | OK as proposed. — Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21 (HC1) |

| US-04-Q-06 | **[Blocks HC1]** "Existing e2e tests keep passing without being loosened": which assertions change, and is the rewrite of §11.1 acceptable? Some tests assert native elements by definition (component test "every field type renders its native control": `tagName: 'SELECT'`, `type: 'date'`; `HTMLSelectElement.options`; `toHaveValue('CC')` on a select; native date segments in `en-US`). | Without an explicit list, the test-engineer would guess, and a silent weakening (for example `allControls()` no longer seeing selects, so `invalidControls()` misses them) would go unnoticed. | Approve §11.1 as the complete list. Rule: each replaced assertion asserts both what the person sees (shown value, role, name, state) and what is stored (`quote-wizard` value), so it is at least as strong; no test is deleted without a replacement; helpers find custom controls by role (`combobox`, `option`, `dialog`, `grid`, `gridcell`), never by class or id. | OK as proposed. — Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21 (HC1) |

Short names: `static-guards` = `frontend/src/app/static-guards.spec.ts` (extended) or a new
`frontend/src/app/design-guards.spec.ts`; `contrast` = `frontend/src/app/shared/contrast.spec.ts`
(WCAG ratio function and the token pairs); `date-text` = `frontend/src/app/shared/date-text.spec.ts`

component specs; `e2e-us04` = new `frontend/e2e/us-04-design-system.spec.ts`. The test-engineer

| US-04-AC-12 | e2e (bounding boxes at three viewports) | `e2e-us04` |
| US-04-AC-13 | component | `step-indicator`, `wizard-header`, page specs |

| US-04-AC-15 | component (deferred HTTP responses) | `quote-form-page`, `plan-list-page`, `summary-page`, `country-chooser-page` |
